text:
Charlie Coyle is having one of those seasons where everything around him looks better than his own line. Columbus takes 56.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, nearly 11 points better than when he sits, in close to 20 minutes a night. And yet he's pointless in his last five games, with three goals all season on 5.1 expected.

That gap is mostly luck, and our numbers see it at both ends. His own shots are going in at 7.9%, and the Blue Jackets have scored 7.5 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. It's why he sits 512th of 529 skaters in wins added despite playing well. One caution from Evolving-Hockey: last season he played with strong teammates, which flatters on-ice numbers. Still, Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 90th percentile among forwards for setting up shots, and his line leans on dump-ins and the forecheck. At 34, speed isn't his selling point; the chances are. We'd watch whether the finishing catches up.
